fields.name: source_port
fields.description: Port of the sending process; if not used, value of zero is inserted. Assumed to be the port to which a reply should be addressed in absence of other information.

fields.name: destination_port
fields.description: Has a meaning within the context of a particular internet destination address.

fields.name: length
fields.description: Length in octets of this user datagram including the header and the data. Minimum value is eight.

fields.name: checksum
fields.description: 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of a pseudo header of information from the IP header, the UDP header, and the data, padded with zero octets at the end if necessary to make a multiple of two octets. If computed checksum is zero, transmitted as all ones. An all zero transmitted checksum means no checksum was generated.

fields.name: source_address
fields.description: Source address from the IP header, conceptually prefixed to the UDP header for checksum computation.

fields.name: destination_address
fields.description: Destination address from the IP header, used in checksum computation.

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Protocol field from the IP header. UDP is protocol 17 (21 octal).

fields.name: udp_length
fields.description: The UDP length, used in checksum computation. Same as the length field in the UDP header.

parsing_context.name: ip_source_address
parsing_context.description: Source internet address from the IP header, required to compute and verify the UDP checksum via the pseudo header.

parsing_context.name: ip_destination_address
parsing_context.description: Destination internet address from the IP header, required to compute and verify the UDP checksum via the pseudo header.

parsing_context.name: ip_protocol
parsing_context.description: Protocol field from the internet header, required for the UDP pseudo header checksum computation.

helper_functions.name: compute_checksum
helper_functions.description: Compute the 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum over the pseudo header, UDP header, and data, padded with zero octets at the end if necessary to make a multiple of two octets. If the computed checksum is zero, it is transmitted as all ones. An all zero transmitted checksum means the transmitter generated no checksum.
